deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is not a Riemann working sheet. It is the first page of a letter from Richard Dedekind to Heinrich Weber, the editor of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (published 1876). It is filed in the Riemann Nachlass bundle 'R.Modulfunctionen' next to Dedekind's commentary on Riemann's fragments on the modular functions. The previous page ends a Dedekind letter dated Braunschweig, 25 Feb 1876. That letter discusses the numbers (m,n), now called Dedekind sums, and their relation to the Jacobi symbol.

Content of this page, in paraphrase:
- Dedekind is worried that he has heard nothing from Weber for a long time. He hopes illness is not the cause. He consoles himself that Weber is fully occupied finishing 'the work so dear to us both', i.e. the edition of Riemann's Werke.
- He suspects Weber may have run into difficulties carrying out his friendly offer to name Dedekind on the title page.
- He again urges, as in his last letter, that his suggestions on this point be treated as passing ideas. If accepting the offer causes Weber the least inconvenience, then (continued on the next page) 'it goes without saying' that they return to their first arrangement, with Weber as sole editor.

Historically, the printed title reads 'herausgegeben unter Mitwirkung von Richard Dedekind von Heinrich Weber', so the compromise was adopted. There are no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Editorial correspondence (Dedekind to Weber, 1876) about title-page credit for the edition of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke; no mathematical content on this page
results.modern_name: History of the 1876 edition of Riemann's Werke
results.usually_credited_to: Heinrich Weber (editor), with the collaboration of Richard Dedekind

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a personal and editorial letter by Dedekind, not by Riemann, and contains no mathematics. The Dedekind–Weber collaboration on Riemann's Werke and the wording of the title page are well documented.
transcription_corrections: Last word of the page: the image reads 'so versteht' (continuing 'es sich ganz von selbst' on the next page), not 'so verletzt[?]'.
The writer is R. Dedekind (letter to H. Weber, early 1876), not Riemann. The page is correspondence filed with the Modulfunctionen material.
The folio number '44' is an archival foliation mark at the top right, not part of the text.
